$comment: The fence's configuration, written by the factory onboarding from what this repository already uses. People own this file (CODEOWNERS). docs/fence.md explains each field. VS Code: the unit check is a repository-local script written at onboarding (.fence/local/unit-affected.mjs); Electron, layers (npm run valid-layers-check) and full compile stay with VS Code's own CI.
mode: large repository: checks run on the files a change touches, compared with the merge base

checks.title: Lint rules (VS Code's own eslint.config.js, including code-layering and code-import-patterns)
checks.explain: VS Code's own ESLint rules on the changed files, including its layering and import rules. Only findings the change adds count.

checks.title: Type check (changed files, src/tsconfig.json)
checks.explain: The TypeScript compiler on the changed files against VS Code's tsconfig. Only errors the change adds count.

checks.title: Unit tests of affected code (Node: test/common, test/node)
checks.explain: Node unit tests in the test files that import a changed file, run with VS Code's own test setup.

checks.title: Browser unit tests of affected code (Chromium, VS Code's own runner)
checks.hint: Run one: node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --run <file> (after node build/next/build-fast.ts --client-only)
checks.explain: Browser unit tests in the test files that import a changed file, run in Chromium by VS Code's own runner.

$guardMayBeEmpty: Set while onboarding: no guard rule is accepted yet, so the guard enforces nothing. A person removes this once they accept rules in the rules workbench (guard.py --serve).
